# Terms & conditions — `terms.dc.html`

**Shell:** `SPEC-legal-shell.md` · **Sections:** 16 · **Status:** built 4 Aug 2026, wording pending

## 1. Structure

```
01 Who you contract with      09 No-show
02 Scope                      10 Changes & cancellation → cancellation.dc.html governs
03 How a booking is formed    11 Payment
04 Fixed price                12 Complaints
05 Partner carriers           13 Liability
06 Your obligations           14 Force majeure
07 Luggage & child seats      15 Your data → privacy.dc.html
08 Waiting time               16 Governing law & venue
```

Restructured from the archived 21-section document, not reordered cosmetically:

- **The data-processing agreement is lifted out.** Archived §§21–23 embedded a DPA and named a
  third party as a data recipient. Section 15 is a pointer to the privacy policy and is built to
  stay one paragraph long.
- **Cancellation rules are lifted out.** Section 10 states the mechanism and defers every number
  to `cancellation.dc.html`. That is the only way the two documents cannot drift.
- **Waiting and no-show are separated** (08, 09). They were one clause; they are two questions a
  customer asks at different moments.

## 2. Decision flags on the page

| # | Section | Conflict |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 01 | Carrier or intermediary. Archived §2 disclaims the ride; the service pages sell “our drivers”. Both paragraphs and section 05 are built so either answer fits |
| 2 | 04 | The extended-city-stay fee is priced in euro on a Swiss operation |
| 3 | 11 | Terms list Amex/cash/bank transfer; the FAQ lists TWINT/PayPal/Apple Pay |
| 4 | 15 | DPA and the third-party recipient removed — flagged so nobody restores them |

## 3. Slots — 8

Contracting party (01) · subcontracting (05) · refusal of carriage and soiling (06) · refused and
unaccompanied items (07) · escalation and dispute body (12, shares one answer with the imprint) ·
liability (13) · force majeure (14) · venue (16).

Section 13 carries one non-slot sentence that holds whatever the drafting says: no exclusion for
death or personal injury through negligence, and no removal of Swiss consumer rights.

## 4. Tokens — 17

Effective date · version · registered firm name · airport waiting · standard waiting · extra
waiting rate · extra stop fee · city-stay minutes · city-stay fee · oversize item fee · case
dimensions · driver-details lead time · no-show call attempts · payment methods · complaint window
· resolution days · refund payout days.

## 5. Notes

- Prose is short by design: 16 sections of two or three paragraphs read faster than 21 of five,
  and every sentence a lawyer will rewrite is in a slot rather than in the flow.
- Sections 04, 07, 08 use `<ul>` for anything a customer scans for. Nothing is a wall.
- Cross-links out: cancellation (×3), privacy (×2), cookies, imprint, contact, manage-booking.
